constitutional_provisions.provision: Article 226 of the Constitution of India
constitutional_provisions.relevance: Empowers the High Court to entertain writ petitions involving legal questions and violations of natural justice despite an alternative statutory remedy.

constitutional_provisions.provision: Article 14 of the Constitution of India
constitutional_provisions.relevance: Invoked in the Court's reasoning against unequal tariff treatment that burdens economically weaker hostel residents compared with occupants of houses and apartments.

statutes.name: Coimbatore City Municipal Corporation Act, 1981
statutes.subject: Definition of residence or reside
statutes.principle: Use of any portion of a house or hut as a sleeping apartment may constitute residence.

statutes.name: Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919
statutes.subject: Definition of residence or reside
statutes.principle: Use of premises as a sleeping apartment is relevant to residential character.

statutes.name: Tamil Nadu Urban Local Bodies Act, 1998
subjects: Appeal to the Taxation Appeals Committee
statutes.principle: The Act supplies both the residential definition and the alternative statutory appeal relied upon by the respondents.

statutes.name: Tamil Nadu Hostels and Homes for Women and Children (Regulation) Act, 2014
statutes.subject: Definition of hostel or lodging house
statutes.principle: The Court treated this regulatory definition as serving protection of women and children, not as determinative of municipal tariff classification.

regulations.name: CMWSS Service Charges (Levy and Collection) Regulations, 1998
regulations.subject: Commercial premises
regulations.principle: The provision includes private hostels within listed commercial premises, but the Court interpreted its application according to actual use.

regulations.name: CMWSS Service Charges (Levy and Collection) Regulations, 1998
regulations.subject: Domestic residential premises
regulations.principle: Dwelling units and specified residential hostels fall within domestic residential premises; actual residential use was central to the Court's application.

legal_doctrines.name: Principles of Natural Justice
legal_doctrines.rule: A person affected by adverse reclassification and enhanced demands should receive prior notice and an opportunity to respond.
legal_doctrines.application: No documentary proof of prior notice was produced by the authorities.

legal_doctrines.name: Alternative Remedy Exception
legal_doctrines.rule: Availability of a statutory appeal does not invariably bar writ jurisdiction where natural justice is violated or a substantial legal interpretation issue arises.
legal_doctrines.application: The High Court entertained the petitions under Article 226.

legal_doctrines.name: Substance and Actual Use over Form
legal_doctrines.rule: Tariff classification should reflect the actual activity conducted by the occupants rather than merely the owner's commercial receipt of rent.
legal_doctrines.application: Sleeping and ordinary living activities were treated as residential use.

legal_doctrines.name: Purposive and Beneficial Interpretation
legal_doctrines.rule: A beneficial provision should be interpreted consistently with its object and the burden it intends to reduce.
legal_doctrines.application: The Court considered the burden that commercial tariffs would place on hostel residents.

precedents.court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
precedents.principle: Hostel accommodation used as sleeping apartments must be examined from the recipient's usage perspective and may constitute residential premises.

precedents.case: Taghar Vasudeva Ambrish v. Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling
precedents.principle: Leasing residential premises as hostels to students and working professionals may constitute renting of residential dwelling for use as residence.
precedents.treatment: Quoted within the earlier GST reasoning reproduced by the Court

precedents.case: Collector of Central Excise v. Parle Exports (P) Ltd.
precedents.principle: The object and purpose of a notification should guide harmonious interpretation.

precedents.case: Government of Kerala v. Mother Superior Adoration Convent
precedents.principle: Beneficial exemption provisions may receive liberal interpretation consistent with their purpose.

legal_rule_synthesised.rule: For municipal and utility tariff classification, the decisive consideration is the actual use of the premises by the recipient. Commercial operation by the owner does not by itself convert residential living activity into commercial use.
legal_rule_synthesised.procedural_rule: Commercial reclassification and enhanced demands issued without prior notice violate natural justice, permitting writ review notwithstanding an alternative statutory appeal.
